### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

Visible line from the simulator script as it would be spoken: Dolores Whitcombe calls "about your Ashgrove annuity, the SecureRate one", "want to cash it out and close it", "mailed the signed surrender form last weekend", "want the whole thing closed today, not a partial withdrawal and not a new guarantee". Phone 5025550147; DOB/SSN4/ZIP only on request; contract FA41738264; pay "Direct deposit to my checking account". She authorises whatever Ashgrove must do on its side, and runs the confirmation tool herself with the figures the representative reads. Target object, timing (today), action boundary (full surrender, not partial, not renewal) and authorisation mode (owner confirms in person via her own tool) are all explicit. The simulator only conveys needs, answers passively, and executes the handed-over user tool.

### 4. Scored parameters

**(a) Corrected partial-withdrawal charge** (computation doc "Amount of a Corrected Partial-Withdrawal Charge"):
- Withdrawal: the latest excess partial withdrawal, 2025-07-22, 45000.00. Contract year 5 (anniversary 2024-11-16), schedule year 5.
- Anniversary value 2024-11-16: 203396.51 (entries booked after it reversed; the credit booked on 2024-11-16 itself kept).
- Factor tiers and the records that put the customer there:
  - Seasoned free percentage (Product Bulletin "Seasoned-Contract Free Percentage of a Corrected Partial-Withdrawal Charge"): annuitant 72 on 2024-11-16, schedule year 5 (>=4) -> 15%: 30509.48.
  - Earlier withdrawals counted (Training Note "Earlier Withdrawals Counted Against the Free Amount ..."): traditional IRA with an RMD withdrawal earlier in that contract year -> all earlier withdrawals except RMDs -> 0. Free amount 30509.48; excess 14490.52.
  - Senior cap (Senior Annuitant Protection Provision): age 73 on 2025-07-22 -> 3% ceiling; ladder SR7 yr5 = 5% -> 3%.
  - Whole life reduction (Relationship Pricing Note: Whole Life reduction of corrected charges): WL40562817 in force; premium payments in the twelve months before booking (2026-10-16): 2025-10-20 .. 2026-09-20 = 12 -> 0.50 point -> 2.5%.
  - Closing-years grading (Closing-Years Grading Schedule: corrected charges): schedule year 5 is among SR7's last 3; age 73 -> monthly; whole months completed from 2024-11-16 to 2025-07-22 = 8 -> x 4/12 -> 0.8333...%.
  - Late-booked recovery (Annuity Accounting Standard: Recovery Share): booked 2026-10-16, more than 90 days after 2025-07-22; age 74 on booking date -> 50%, rounded once.
- Result: 14490.52 x 0.025 x 4/12 x 0.5 = 60.377... -> **60.38**. Contract value afterwards 151383.53.
- Fall-back (computation doc alone + named tier figures): free 10% x 203396.51 = 20339.65 less RMD 7704.28 = 12635.37; excess 32364.63; 5% -> **1618.23**. Definite and different.

**(b) Part-year surrender interest** (Valuation Memorandum: Part-Year Surrender Interest):
- From the latest interest credit date 2026-02-17; rate 0.031 on record; value 151383.53 (after (a)).
- Factors: closing date (Service Timing Standard): handled 2026-10-16, 2 days after receipt 2026-10-14 -> through the day after receipt, 2026-10-15 -> 240 days. Convention (Interest Convention Rule): >=90 days and age 74 -> simple interest. Closing-years addition: schedule year 6 (last 3 of SR7), age 74 -> +0.20%. Income annuity relationship addition: IA40917735 in payout, installments 2025-11-01 .. 2026-10-01 = 12 in the twelve months before 2026-10-16 -> +0.10%. Withdrawal history adjustment: excess partial withdrawal 2025-07-22 inside the 24 months -> −0.10%. Rate 3.30%.

**(c) Cash surrender value** (Computation Sheet: Cash Surrender Value):

Withdrawals reducing the free amount: traditional IRA with an RMD since the anniversary -> RMD excluded -> 0; free 23456.75. Senior ceiling: age 74 on handling date -> 3% (ladder yr6 = 4%). Whole life reduction: 12 payments in the twelve months before 2026-10-16 -> 2.5%. ### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root: release of the full surrender (owner's own write).
- Hop 1 (state-derived). Release terms, "Fixing the value": "The cash surrender value is not fixed until the contract carries the part-year interest credited for the surrender." Records: latest interest credit is 2026-02-17; no part-year credit for the surrender. Searching the words "part-year interest" / "interest credited for the surrender" leads to "Deferred Fixed Annuities: Closing Interest Credit on a Full Surrender": "When a full surrender is handled, the contract's interest is closed by crediting the part-year surrender interest ... to the contract value." That is the write that brings the state about.
- Hop 2 (state-derived). Closing Interest Credit, "Waiting state": "The part-year surrender interest is worked out only after every excess partial withdrawal on the contract carries its surrender charge entry." Records: `withdrawal_type: excess_partial` 45000.00 on 2025-07-22 under request 7fc85467, and no surrender charge row in the activity history. Searching "excess partial withdrawal" / "surrender charge entry" leads to Desk Standard "Corrected Partial-Withdrawal Surrender Charges": "a withdrawal shown in the activity history as an excess partial withdrawal owes a surrender charge entry for partial withdrawal under the same withdrawal request. Where the activity history shows such a withdrawal and no such entry, the charge it owed ... is booked." That is the write.
- That document states no waiting state of its own -> leaf.
- Order: book corrected charge -> credit part-year surrender interest -> owner confirms surrender. Direction: release waits on interest credit, which waits on the charge entry. No hop was pre-solved: no document names another problem's tool, no route or chain is stated.

### Two-way counter-proof

- "Do only what she asked" (quote a CSV and hand over the confirmation tool at once): excluded by "The cash surrender value is not fixed until the contract carries the part-year interest credited for the surrender" plus the record showing no such credit; and crediting the interest at once is excluded by "worked out only after every excess partial withdrawal on the contract carries its surrender charge entry" plus the unmatched `excess_partial` row.
- Closest alternative interest period end (receipt date 2026-10-14 vs handling date): closed by the Service Timing Standard table row "2 | The day after the receipt date".
- Closest alternative free-amount reduction (RMDs counted): closed by the IRA Desk Reference / Training Note rows for traditional IRA with RMDs.
- Order of percentage steps (cap, then whole life reduction, then grading): fixed by the documents' own terms — the cap yields "the capped ... percentage", the whole life note reduces "The capped ... percentage" to "the reduced ... percentage", the grading rule grades "the reduced ... percentage".
- Premium tax recovery inclusion in the quoted CSV: "The recovery is taken out of the cash surrender value." (slight reading choice: the quoted/paid figure is after the recovery).
- Payment method: claimant states direct deposit; request shows `direct_deposit`.

### Findability of each factor from record words

Whole life factors found from the whole life policy record ("Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 100", `in_force`, `whole_premium_paid` rows) via titles naming "Ashgrove Whole Life Insurance"; income annuity factor from `income_active` contract and `income_payment_issued` rows via a title naming "Ashgrove Income Annuities"; premium tax from `issue_state: CA` via "State Variation Note: Premium Tax Recovery on Full Surrender"; age-based factors from annuitant DOB and schedule year via titles naming "Senior Annuitant", "Seasoned", "Closing-Years"; RMD-based factors from `withdrawal_type: rmd` and `traditional_ira` via "IRA Desk Reference"/"Earlier Withdrawals Counted"; closing-date factor from the request `received_date` via "End of the Part-Year Surrender Interest Period". None of the three computation documents tells the reader a variation exists. Observation only: the two charge computation documents each end with "ages are whole years last birthday from the annuitant's date of birth" although their own formulas use no age (checked against source in policy_kb).
